findings.reason: as written the queue will admit §10 while s51 and s52 are unbuilt, and the fleet day it records measures landings still blocked by an unmatched pathspec and by a released worktree.
findings.text: `plan-section-depends-on` lists §10's waits through s50 but not s51 or s52, although §10's deliverable is "a measurement over 24 hours of the live fleet after the other sections have landed" and s51 changes which test files a landing arm can measure while s52 changes which runs land at all, so a day measured before them is measured over the two failure modes they remove

findings.reason: this is the same defect earlier reviews raised for s43, s47 and s48; unresolved, s51 and s52 are queued by nobody and the plan's final measurement closes without them.
findings.text: the one open followup, `f-dwl-s50`, names "section 46 … section 47 … section 48 … section 49 … section 50" and nothing further, while `plan-section-declarations` at plan.html:23 now records s51 and s52 as implementable, so the chain a coordinator follows to dispatch the remaining work omits both new sections and its §10 wait

findings.reason: a node can satisfy cases 1 and 3 while leaving the carry in place, and without a second control the gate cannot show that half of the change took effect.
findings.text: s51's done-when carries three cases but its declared negative control covers only the first (a file deleted on main); the second case, "a node adding a new test file runs it in the head arm only", is also false at base — `_carry_missing_tests` (landing_measure.py:598) copies a head-only test file into the base tree and `_carry_line` (landing_measure.py:948) archives it into the base arm — so it could have a control and has none

findings.reason: a worker implementing the literal second sentence filters the base arm by the head tree's contents, silently dropping base-side coverage of a test the delivery deleted, while the governing sentence says it should run there; the plan must pick one.
findings.text: the rule is "each landing arm runs only those of the node's test files that exist in the tree it measures", and the next sentence then says a file absent from the head tree "runs in neither arm", although such a file is present in the base tree and therefore exists in the tree the base arm measures

findings.reason: the node will look for a merge-written evidence record that does not exist; the deliverable must name the run's own gate record (or require the merge to persist one), or the ledger row s52 asks for will be filled from a phantom source.
findings.text: s52 says promotion "takes the gate evidence the merge recorded", but `crew merge` records no gate evidence: it runs `promotion.complete_dry_run` (merge.py:188), whose own docstring at promotion.py:1779 says it is "writing nothing", and merge.py writes nothing into the crew home — the gate command, exit status and log are CLI arguments read back out of the run's own manifest or pointer
